title: West Montrose Covered Bridge rehabilitation design approved
subtitle: Committee also heard the e-scooter pilot's first-year results and discussed Grand River Transit bus stop design guidelines.
overview: The Planning and Works Committee recommended approving the rehabilitation design concept for the West Montrose Covered Bridge in Woolwich {{vote:m3}}. The recommendation also directs staff to file the Notice of Completion for the Class Environmental Assessment, place the study report on the public record for 30 days, and work with the Township on amendments to the bridge's heritage designation by-law. Council still has to adopt it.

The committee also received the 2023 update on the shared micromobility (e-scooter) program, after a presentation from the operator. It was received for information with the consent agenda {{vote:m2}}. Staff said the program will relaunch in April. Councillors raised parking, impaired riding, helmets, pricing and expanding the service area.

Grand River Transit's bus stop design guidelines were pulled from the consent agenda for discussion and received for information. Staff said the wording about MobilityPLUS will be corrected, and that the capital budget for stop improvements limits how quickly accessible pads and shelters can be added. Staff said the business plan will look at speeding this up.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the rehabilitation design concept for the bridge in Woolwich, filing the Notice of Completion, a 30-day public record period, and working with the Township on heritage by-law amendments.
The committee received the report on the 2023 e-scooter riding season for information as part of the consent agenda.
The committee received the Grand River Transit bus stop design guidelines for information, with the report discussed after being pulled from the consent agenda.

debate: On e-scooters, councillors raised messy or crowded parking and bikes left lying over. The operator pointed to parking mats, corrals, an app feature that checks the parking spot, and smaller parking areas.

Councillors raised concerns about impaired riding and helmet use. The operator described a late-evening reaction game, safety ambassadors and helmet incentives. It said mandatory helmet locks tend to cause helmets to be discarded, and that enforcement tools are limited.

On pricing, a councillor asked about affordability. The operator described monthly, weekly and three-day passes, a 50% discount for those facing financial hardship and a 30% student discount. It said it is reviewing pay-as-you-go pricing.

On bus stops, councillors asked about waste receptacles, benches in rural areas and shelters. Staff said the guidelines lead into case-by-case discussions and that the capital budget would take about 15 years to reach basic accessibility on pads. They said the 2025 to 2030 business plan will look at accelerating this.

On the bridge, councillors asked about heritage status and funding. Staff said the bridge is designated under the Ontario Heritage Act and that an all-wood design is more heritage-like than the original steel-girder concept. Staff said a delegate's remaining concerns are mostly minor and can be handled in detailed design.
